subject: English
passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Women scientists made significant contributions to the Manhattan Project during World War II.
• Physicist Lise Meitner, one of the project's key researchers, was a nuclear physicist who had worked on atomic fission theory.
• Chemist Marie Curie had been a renowned researcher who won Nobel Prizes for her work on radioactivity.
• Meitner provided crucial theoretical insights that helped scientists understand the nuclear chain reaction process.
• Curie's earlier research on radium and polonium formed the foundation for much of the project's experimental work.
prompt: The student wants to compare the two scientists' contributions to atomic research. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

choices.A: Although Meitner provided crucial theoretical insights about nuclear chain reactions, Curie's earlier research on radium and polonium formed the foundation for experimental work.
choices.B: Meitner and Curie contributed to atomic research in different ways; Curie, for example, conducted groundbreaking research on radium and polonium.
choices.C: Meitner worked in nuclear physics and contributed to the Manhattan Project, while Curie was a chemist who won Nobel Prizes for radioactivity research.
choices.D: Many women scientists, including Curie and Meitner, advanced our understanding of atomic science, but they worked in different time periods.

explanation:
Choice A is the best answer. The sentence compares the two scientists' contributions to atomic research: Meitner provided crucial theoretical insights about nuclear chain reactions, whereas Curie's earlier research formed the foundation for experimental work.

Why B is incorrect:

Choice B is incorrect. While it acknowledges that the two scientists both contributed to atomic research, it doesn't indicate what Meitner did, so no comparison is made.
